meta.description: Priya Vishwanathan: thirty-five years with IHCL; she helped build and scale amã Stays & Trails. Advisory for homestay and hotel owners, growing groups and boards, and conversations on service and leadership.

sections.name: Priya <t>Vishwanathan</t>
sections.sub: Helping owners of hotels and homestays build places <t>guests remember.</t>

sections.label: The practice
sections.statement: The rigour of a great hotel company, <t>at the scale of each property.</t>
body: Thirty-five years inside IHCL, the company behind the Taj: from a duty manager’s desk at St. James’ Court in London, through fifteen years in Business Excellence, to helping build and scale amã Stays & Trails into a distinctive hospitality brand.
Today, an independent advisory practice for owners of homestays and hotels, for groups in growth, and for the boards that guide them.
sections.sign: अतिथि देवो भव · the guest is god

sections.label: Engagements
sections.title: Where the work <t>usually begins.</t>
items: A family home that could welcome guests, but has never been run as a business.
A beautiful property whose guests do not come back.
A team that serves well on good days, and only on good days.
A group that is growing faster than its standards.
A new hotel or homestay, still on paper, that needs an operator’s eye before it opens.
A board or founder who wants someone at the table who has run hotels.

sections.label: Advisory
sections.title: Four areas <t>of practice.</t>
sections.lede: Each grounded in a chapter of the IHCL years.

items.for: Owners of homestays, villas & boutique hotels
items.d: Concept, the story of the house, pre-opening and standards that still feel like a home.
Common standards, quality systems and the measures that make a portfolio consistent without making it identical.
items.from: Grounded in fifteen years of Business Excellence

items.d: An operator’s eye at the table: growth, brand, people and the decisions a hotel cannot undo.
items.from: Grounded in thirty-five years of leadership at IHCL

items.d: Masterclasses, panels and award juries. Team capability programmes run through HOSPI Sigma.

sections.label: The defining chapter
sections.title: amã Stays <t>& Trails.</t>
sections.body: Families brought homes their parents had left them. Each was heard out, kept true to itself, and joined to a brand that now spans India.

img.alt: A planter’s bungalow veranda at dawn (illustrative)

items.k: Senior Assessor, Tata Business Excellence Model.
items.t: Eight external assessments of Tata companies against the framework every Tata company is measured by.
items.d: The model is set out on the [career page](/vishwanathan/track#tbem).

items.k: From isolated hotels to one organisation.
items.t: Fifteen years in Business Excellence, part of the work that gave IHCL structured standards across its hotels.
items.d: Customer-satisfaction work across more than 100 hotels.

items.t: Regional jury (South) for the 10th BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Awards, alongside leaders of WelcomHeritage, Turnstone and Encovate.
items.d: Knowledge partner: Indian School of Hospitality.

sections.lead: Written before a conversation on Inspire Someone Today, 2026.
sections.q: “Success is not measured by how many people know your name. It is measured by how many people are better because they crossed your path.”

sections.label: In conversation
sections.title: On the <t>record.</t>
sections.lede: Two long-form conversations recorded in 2026: one with a fellow hotelier, one on a life in hospitality.

items.t: Hotels Are Solving the Wrong Problem
items.d: Data over instinct, improvement without overspending, Business Excellence at IHCL, and why a struggling culture is easier to fix than a struggling business.

items.t: How Many People Are Better Because They Crossed Your Path?
items.d: Day three at the Taj, homestays built with the families who own them, service without servility, and leaving at the top.
